’Opakapaka case study: benchmarking opal against Stock Synthesis 3

Introduction

This vignette documents the configuration, fitting, and cross-platform benchmarking of an opal stock assessment model for ’opakapaka (Pristipomoides filamentosus), a Hawaiian deepwater snapper. The reference model was built in Stock Synthesis 3 (SS3 v3.30.19) as part of the Opaka_simulation project, which provides both an operating model (OM) and an estimation model (EM).

The primary objective is to verify that opal’s population dynamics engine reproduces SS3’s spawning biomass trajectory when given identical inputs. A secondary objective is to demonstrate model fit to multiple data sources: index and length composition data.

The model covers the historical period 1949–2023 with three fleets: a commercial fishery (Comm), a non-commercial fishery (Non_comm), and a research fishery survey (ResFish).

Load inputs

Load the opal package and the RTMB dependency. The tidyverse package is used for data manipulation and plotting.

library(tidyverse)
library(opal)
library(RTMB)

theme_set(theme_bw())

The bundled data object opaka_data contains all biological parameters, catch and CPUE observations, length structure, and prior specifications needed for the opakapaka assessment model.

SS3 indexes ages from 0 to 43 (44 age classes), while opal uses 1-based internal indexing. To ensure the growth curve, survivorship, and all age-structured biology vectors align correctly with SS3, we set A1 = 0 (anchoring the Schnute growth parameterization at biological age 0) and redefine age_a accordingly. The min_age field is passed to get_growth() so that the age sequence starts at 0 rather than 1.

data(opaka_data)
data <- opaka_data
if (is.null(data$n_index)) data$n_index <- 2L
names(data)

# remove priors
data$priors <- NULL

# set ages to anchor growth curve (since SS3 indexs from 0 to 43, but opal uses 1-based indexing)
data$A1 <- 0
data$A2 <- data$A1 + (data$n_age-1)
data$min_age <- 0
ages <- data$age_a <- seq(data$min_age, by = 1, length.out = data$n_age)

Key dimensions of the data:

cat("Number of ages:", data$n_age, "\n")
cat("Number of years:", data$n_year, "\n")
cat("Number of fisheries:", data$n_fishery, "\n")
cat("Number of length bins:", data$n_len, "\n")

Biological inputs

Natural mortality is constant across all ages at M = 0.135 yr−1^{-1}. Maturity follows a length-based logistic curve with Mat50 = 40.7 cm. The length-weight relationship uses a = 1.75 ×10−5\times 10^{-5} and b = 2.99. Fecundity is proportional to body weight (SS3 option 1 with a = 1, b = 0).

The sex ratio vector (sex_ratio) is set to 1.0 at all ages. Although SS3 applies a female fraction of 0.5 when computing SSB, this scaling is already implicit in opal’s B0B_0 parameterization: opal defines B0B_0 as female-only spawning biomass (matching SS3’s reported SSB_Virgin), so the per-recruit spawning potential does not require an additional sex-ratio multiplier. See the dynamics diagnostic section for further discussion.

# Natural mortality
ggplot(data.frame(age = ages, M = data$M), aes(x = age, y = M)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point(size = 0.8) +
  labs(x = "Age (opal internal)", y = "M (annual rate)",
       title = "Natural Mortality-at-Age")

# Maturity at length
len_mid <- seq(data$len_bin_start + data$len_bin_width / 2,
               by = data$len_bin_width, length.out = data$n_len)
ggplot(data.frame(length = len_mid, maturity = data$maturity),
       aes(x = length, y = maturity)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Length (cm)", y = "Maturity",
       title = "Maturity-at-Length (logistic, Mat50 = 40.7 cm)")

# define sex ratio vector
data$sex_ratio <- rep(1, data$n_age)

Length composition data

Length composition observations are loaded from the bundled opaka_lf long-format data object and transformed into model-ready arrays. Data are available for two fleets: Comm (fleet 1, 1949–2023) and ResFish (fleet 3, 2017–2023). Fleet 2 (Non_comm) has no length composition data.

data(opaka_lf)

# Pivot to wide format: one row per fishery x timestep, bins as columns
lf_wide <- opaka_lf %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(fishery, year, month, ts),
    names_from = bin,
    values_from = value,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  arrange(fishery, ts)

# Define variance adjustment scalars for each fishery
var_adjust_scalars <- 1 / rep(1, data$n_fishery)

data <- prep_lf_data(data, lf_wide,
                     lf_keep_fisheries = c(1, 3),
                     lf_var_adjust = var_adjust_scalars,
                     lf_addtocomp = 1e-10)

Set up SS3-style bias ramps

SS3 applies a bias adjustment ramp to the lognormal recruitment correction term, following Methot and Taylor (2011). The ramp reduces the correction −0.5⋅σR2-0.5 \cdot \sigma_R^2 in years where recruitment deviations are poorly informed by data, preventing the mean-unbiasing from introducing systematic bias when deviations are estimated imprecisely. The ramp is defined by four control years (ascending start, plateau start, plateau end, descending end) and a maximum bias adjustment fraction.

Two ramps are constructed: one for the initial age cohorts (birth years 1906–1949, applied via init_bias_adj_a) and one for the time-series cohorts (1949–2023, applied via bias_adj_y). Both use the SS3 EM’s estimated ramp parameters.

# 1. INITIAL COHORTS (1906 to 1949)
# Data ages are 1-based, so 1949 - (age - 1) gives the birth year.
# Age_a = 1 (bio age 0) -> Born in 1949.
# Age_a = 44 (bio age 43) -> Born in 1906.
init_cohort_years <- 1949 - (data$age_a - 1)

data$init_bias_adj_a <- get_bias_adj_vector(
  years = init_cohort_years,
  do_rec_bias_ramp = 1,
  bias_years = c(1931, 1974, 2021.88, 2022.43),
  max_bias_adj = 0.869
)

# 2. TIME SERIES COHORTS (1950 to 2024)
# Because rdev_y[1] generates recruits for year 2 (1950),
# the time-series bias ramp must evaluate 1950 to 2024.
calendar_years <- (1949-1) + data$years

data$bias_adj_y <- get_bias_adj_vector(
  years = calendar_years,
  do_rec_bias_ramp = 1,
  bias_years = c(1931, 1974, 2021.88, 2022.43),
  max_bias_adj = 0.869
)

Model setup

Parameters

Define the initial parameter values. Growth parameters (log_L1, log_L2, log_k, log_CV1, log_CV2) and selectivity (par_sel) are initialised from the SS3 estimates. Load these from the bundled opaka_parameters data object:

data(opaka_parameters)

# Route 1949 dev to biological age 0, which is index 1 in opal's 1-based age vector.
# In the SS3 vector, rdev_y[1] is the 1949 deviation; here it seeds the initial
# age-0 cohort, while later years are shifted into the modeled rdev_y time series.
init_rdev_a <- rep(0.0, data$n_age)
init_rdev_a = rev(c(0.0206807,0.00321579,0.00372620,0.0043174,0.00500263,0.00579674,0.00671727,0.00778422,0.00902081,0.0104539,0.0121143,0.0140375,0.0162641,0.0188404,0.0218182,0.0252561,0.0292182,0.0337726,0.0389898,0.0449362,0.0516662,0.0592049,0.0675236,0.0764992,0.0858443,0.0950047,0.102706,0.107687,0.107712,0.0998349,0.0808137,0.0482339,0.00234443,-0.0517563,-0.102395,-0.131458,-0.121101,-0.0714826,-0.00742166,-0.0109308,-0.0385029,0.0366483,0.0165105,-0.166906))
# Remaining initial ages start at equilibrium and are estimated via init_rdev_a.
init_rdev_a[1] <- opaka_parameters$rdev_y[1]

# Shift 1950-2023 into rdev_y and add 0.0 for terminal/forecast year 2024
rdev_y_shifted <- c(opaka_parameters$rdev_y[2:length(opaka_parameters$rdev_y)], 0.0)

parameters <- list(
  log_B0 = 9,
  log_h = as.numeric(opaka_parameters$log_h),
  log_sigma_r = as.numeric(opaka_parameters$log_sigma_r),
  log_cpue_q = as.numeric(opaka_parameters$log_cpue_q),
  log_cpue_tau = rep(log(0.1),data$n_index),
  log_cpue_omega = as.numeric(rep(opaka_parameters$log_cpue_omega, data$n_index)),
  log_lf_tau = as.numeric(log(rep(0.1, data$n_fishery))),
  log_L1 = as.numeric(opaka_parameters$log_L1),
  log_L2 = as.numeric(opaka_parameters$log_L2),
  log_k = as.numeric(opaka_parameters$log_k),
  log_CV1 = as.numeric(opaka_parameters$log_CV1),
  log_CV2 = as.numeric(opaka_parameters$log_CV2),
  par_sel = as.matrix(opaka_parameters$par_sel),
  log_init_F_f = c(log(0.0119122), rep(log(1e-8), data$n_fishery - 1)),
  rdev_y = rdev_y_shifted,
  init_rdev_a = init_rdev_a
)

# convert ss3 parameters to opal parameters (selectivity)
parameters$par_sel = convert_ss3_selex_to_rtmb(parameters$par_sel, data$sel_type_f, data$len_mid)

Priors

Priors are specified using get_priors(). The data object already contains prior center values for growth parameters:

data$priors <- get_priors(parameters = parameters, data = data)
evaluate_priors(parameters = parameters, priors = data$priors)

Parameter map

RTMB’s map mechanism controls which parameters are estimated vs. fixed. Parameters mapped to factor(NA) are held at their initial values.

The estimated parameter set includes log_B0 (unfished spawning biomass), log_cpue_q (catchability for each CPUE index), rdev_y (annual recruitment deviations), init_rdev_a (initial age-structure deviations), and selected selectivity parameters for the Comm and ResFish fleets. Steepness, σR\sigma_R, growth parameters, and some selectivity parameters are fixed at values from the SS3 OM.

map_sel <- matrix(NA, nrow(parameters$par_sel), ncol(parameters$par_sel))
# map_sel[1,1:2 ] <- c(1,2) # Comm fleet selectivity parameters
# map_sel[3,c(1,4,6) ] <- c(3,4,5) # Comm fleet selectivity parameters
map_sel = as.vector(map_sel)

map_lf_tau <- rep(NA, length(parameters$log_lf_tau))

map <- list(
  # log_B0 = factor(NA),
  log_h = factor(NA),
  log_sigma_r = factor(NA),
  # log_cpue_q = factor(NA),
  log_cpue_tau = as.factor(rep(NA, data$n_index)),
  log_cpue_omega = as.factor(rep(NA, data$n_index)),
  log_lf_tau = factor(map_lf_tau),
  log_L1  = factor(NA),
  log_L2  = factor(NA),
  log_k   = factor(NA),
  log_CV1 = factor(NA),
  log_CV2 = factor(NA),
  par_sel = factor(map_sel),
  # log_init_F_f = as.factor(c(1, rep(NA, data$n_fishery - 1))),
  log_init_F_f = rep(factor(NA), data$n_fishery),
  # init_rdev_a = rep(factor(NA), data$n_age)
  init_rdev_a = as.factor(seq_len(data$n_age)),
  rdev_y = as.factor(seq_len(length(parameters$rdev_y)))
)

Build the AD object

Using the data, the parameters, the parameter map, and the model (opal_model), the AD object is created using RTMB’s MakeADFun function:

data$lf_switch <- 0 # skip length comps initially (removal only)
# data$lf_switch <- 1L # multinomial likelihood
# data$cpue_switch <- 0L
# Can set random = "rdev_y" to treat recruitment deviations as random effects, but start with fixed effects for simplicity
obj <- MakeADFun(func = cmb(opal_model, data), parameters = parameters, map = map)
unique(names(obj$par))
obj$fn()
obj$gr()

Inspect initial model outputs:

plot(obj$report()$spawning_biomass_y, type = "l",
     xlab = "Time step", ylab = "Spawning biomass",
     main = "Initial spawning biomass trajectory")

Parameter bounds 

Lwr <- rep(-Inf, length(obj$par))
Upr <- rep(Inf, length(obj$par))
Lwr[grep("log_B0", names(obj$par))] <- log(1)
Upr[grep("log_B0", names(obj$par))] <- log(exp(22))
Lwr[grep("log_cpue_q", names(obj$par))] <- log(0.001)
Upr[grep("log_cpue_q", names(obj$par))] <- log(10)
Lwr[grep("rdev_y", names(obj$par))] <- rep(-5, length(grep("rdev_y", names(obj$par))))
Upr[grep("rdev_y", names(obj$par))] <- rep(5, length(grep("rdev_y", names(obj$par))))
Lwr[grep("init_rdev_a", names(obj$par))] <- rep(-5, data$n_age)
Upr[grep("init_rdev_a", names(obj$par))] <- rep(5, data$n_age)
bounds <- data.frame(par = names(obj$par), lower = Lwr, upper = Upr)

ASPM

The Age-Structured Production Model (ASPM) is the simplest opal variant: all recruitment deviations are fixed at zero, so recruitment follows the Beverton-Holt stock-recruitment curve exactly. The only estimated parameters are the population scale (B0B_0) and CPUE catchabilities. The model fits the two CPUE indices only; length compositions are not included.

Setup 

# Build data object for ASPM: inherit lf_switch = 0, no sel_fa_external at this point
data_aspm <- data
data_aspm$cpue_switch <- 1L   # explicitly fit CPUE

# Parameters: all recruitment deviations fixed at 0
parameters_aspm <- parameters
parameters_aspm$rdev_y     <- rep(0.0, length(parameters$rdev_y))
parameters_aspm$init_rdev_a <- rep(0.0, data$n_age)

# Map: fix rdev_y and init_rdev_a in addition to ASPM-R fixed params
map_aspm <- map
map_aspm$rdev_y     <- factor(rep(NA, length(parameters_aspm$rdev_y)))
map_aspm$init_rdev_a <- factor(rep(NA, data$n_age))

obj_aspm <- MakeADFun(func = cmb(opal_model, data_aspm),
                      parameters = parameters_aspm, map = map_aspm)
unique(names(obj_aspm$par))
obj_aspm$fn()

Parameter bounds 

Lwr_aspm <- rep(-Inf, length(obj_aspm$par))
Upr_aspm <- rep( Inf, length(obj_aspm$par))
Lwr_aspm[grep("log_B0",     names(obj_aspm$par))] <- log(1)
Upr_aspm[grep("log_B0",     names(obj_aspm$par))] <- log(exp(22))
Lwr_aspm[grep("log_cpue_q", names(obj_aspm$par))] <- log(0.001)
Upr_aspm[grep("log_cpue_q", names(obj_aspm$par))] <- log(10)

Optimisation 

control <- list(eval.max = 10000, iter.max = 10000)
opt_aspm <- nlminb(start = obj_aspm$par, objective = obj_aspm$fn,
                   gradient = obj_aspm$gr, lower = Lwr_aspm, upper = Upr_aspm,
                   control = control)
opt_aspm <- nlminb(start = opt_aspm$par, objective = obj_aspm$fn,
                   gradient = obj_aspm$gr, lower = Lwr_aspm, upper = Upr_aspm,
                   control = control)
opt_aspm <- nlminb(start = opt_aspm$par, objective = obj_aspm$fn,
                   gradient = obj_aspm$gr, lower = Lwr_aspm, upper = Upr_aspm,
                   control = control)
cat("Convergence:", opt_aspm$convergence, "\n")
cat("Max gradient:", max(abs(obj_aspm$gr())), "\n")
obj_aspm$report()$lp_prior
sum(obj_aspm$report()$lp_cpue)

Check that all parameters are estimable using the check_estimability function:

check_estimability(obj = obj_aspm)

Parameter table 

get_par_table(obj_aspm, parameters_aspm, map_aspm,
              lower = Lwr_aspm, upper = Upr_aspm, grad_tol = 1e-2, digits = 2L)

CPUE fit 

cpue_df_aspm <- data_aspm$cpue_data %>%
  mutate(pred = obj_aspm$report()$cpue_pred)

ggplot(cpue_df_aspm, aes(x = ts, y = value)) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = factor(index)), shape = 21, size = 3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = pred, colour = factor(index)), linewidth = 1.25) +
  labs(x = "Time step", y = "CPUE", colour = "Index", fill = "Index",
       title = "ASPM: observed vs predicted CPUE") +
  scale_colour_brewer(type = "qual", palette = "Dark2") +
  scale_fill_brewer(type = "qual", palette = "Dark2") +
  theme_minimal()

ASPM-R

The ASPM-R model extends the ASPM by freely estimating annual recruitment deviations (rdev_y) and initial age-structure deviations (init_rdev_a), allowing the model to track interannual recruitment variability. It fits the CPUE index only; length compositions remain off.

Optimise using the nlminb function, run twice to ensure convergence:

control <- list(eval.max = 10000, iter.max = 10000)
opt <- nlminb(start = obj$par, objective = obj$fn, gradient = obj$gr,
              hessian = obj$he, lower = Lwr, upper = Upr, control = control)
opt <- nlminb(start = opt$par, objective = obj$fn, gradient = obj$gr,
              hessian = obj$he, lower = Lwr, upper = Upr, control = control)
opt <- nlminb(start = opt$par, objective = obj$fn, gradient = obj$gr,
              hessian = obj$he, lower = Lwr, upper = Upr, control = control)
obj$fn()
max(abs(obj$gr()))
obj$report()$lp_prior
obj$report()$lp_penalty
obj$report()$lp_rec
sum(obj$report()$lp_cpue)
sum(obj$report()$lp_lf)

Compare initial and estimated parameter values:

get_par_table(obj, parameters, map, lower = Lwr, upper = Upr, grad_tol = 1e-2, digits = 2L)

Diagnostics

Check that all parameters are estimable using the check_estimability function:

check_estimability(obj = obj)

Look for any parameters with high correlations (absolute correlation > 0.95) using the get_cor_pairs function:

get_cor_pairs(obj = obj, threshold = 0.95)

Calculate standard deviations of all model parameters:

Report <- RTMB::sdreport(obj)

Data fits

The CPUE series is set up using RTMB’s OBS mechanism inside the model, which allows simulation via obj$simulate().

set.seed(42)
sims <- replicate(20, obj$simulate()$cpue_log_obs, simplify = FALSE)

# again include index so points and lines are drawn per series
cpue_df <- data$cpue_data %>%
  mutate(pred = obj$report()$cpue_pred)

# plot simulated replicates with index grouping
base_plot <- ggplot(cpue_df, aes(x = ts, y = value)) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = factor(index)),shape=21,size=3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = pred, color = factor(index)),linewidth=1.25) +
  labs(x = "Time step", y = "CPUE", color = "Index", fill = "Index",
       title = "Simulated vs observed CPUE (20 replicates)") +
  scale_color_brewer(type = "qual", palette = "Dark2") +
  scale_fill_brewer(type = "qual", palette = "Dark2") +
  theme_minimal()

# add simulated series in gray
sim_df <- map_dfr(sims, ~ data.frame(ts = data$cpue_data$ts,
                                     index = as.factor(data$cpue_data$index),
                                     sim = exp(.x)), .id = "iter")

base_plot +
  geom_line(data = sim_df, aes(x = ts, y = sim, group = iter,color=index), alpha = 0.5)

The length compositions are also set up using RTMB’s OBS mechanism inside the model, which allows simulation via obj$simulate().

if (data$lf_switch == 0) {
  cat("Length composition likelihood is switched off (lf_switch = 0), so no predicted length compositions to show.\n")
} else {
  lf_rep <- obj$report()
  lf_pred <- lf_rep$lf_pred
  nbins <- data$lf_maxbin[1] - data$lf_minbin[1] + 1

  # Name the list elements and columns
  names(lf_pred) <- data$lf_fishery_f
  for (k in seq_along(lf_pred)) colnames(lf_pred[[k]]) <- data$len_mid

  # Helper: convert a flat OBS vector back to list-of-matrices (proportions)
  flat_to_list <- function(v, lf_n_f, nbins) {
    out <- vector("list", length(lf_n_f))
    offset <- 0L
    for (k in seq_along(lf_n_f)) {
      m <- matrix(v[(offset + 1):(offset + lf_n_f[k] * nbins)], nrow = lf_n_f[k], ncol = nbins, byrow = TRUE)
      # Normalise each row to proportions
      rs <- rowSums(m)
      rs[rs == 0] <- 1
      out[[k]] <- m / rs
      offset <- offset + lf_n_f[k] * nbins
    }
    out
  }

  # Split year index by fishery (must match length of lf_year)
  lf_year_list <- split(data$lf_year, data$lf_fishery)

  # ---- Predicted: long data frame ----
  df_pred <- map_dfr(seq_along(lf_pred), function(i) {
    m <- lf_pred[[i]]
    yrs <- lf_year_list[[i]]
    as.data.frame.table(m, responseName = "pred", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
      rename(id = Var1, length = Var2) %>%
      mutate(fishery = names(lf_pred)[i],
             id = as.integer(factor(id, levels = unique(id))),
             year = yrs[id],
             length = as.numeric(length))
  })

  # ---- Observed: long data frame ----
  df_obs <- data.frame(data$lf_obs_in)
  names(df_obs) <- data$len_mid
  df_obs <- df_obs %>%
    mutate(year = data$lf_year, fishery = as.character(data$lf_fishery)) %>%
    group_by(fishery) %>%
    mutate(id = row_number()) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = -c(year, fishery, id), names_to = "length", values_to = "obs") %>%
    mutate(length = as.numeric(length))

  # ---- Simulations: generate n_sim draws and convert to long format ----
  n_sim <- 5
  df_sim_all <- map_dfr(seq_len(n_sim), function(s) {
    # Determine which OBS vector was active based on lf_switch
    sim <- obj$simulate()
    if (data$lf_switch == 1) {
      sim_vec <- sim$lf_obs_flat
    } else if (data$lf_switch == 2) {
      sim_vec <- sim$lf_obs_prop
    } else {
      sim_vec <- sim$lf_obs_ints
    }
    sim_list <- flat_to_list(sim_vec, data$lf_n_f, nbins)
    names(sim_list) <- data$lf_fishery_f
    for (k in seq_along(sim_list)) colnames(sim_list[[k]]) <- data$len_mid
    map_dfr(seq_along(sim_list), function(i) {
      m <- sim_list[[i]]
      yrs <- lf_year_list[[i]]
      as.data.frame.table(m, responseName = "sim", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
        rename(id = Var1, length = Var2) %>%
        mutate(fishery = names(sim_list)[i],
               id = as.integer(factor(id, levels = unique(id))),
               year = yrs[id],
               length = as.numeric(length),
               sim_id = s)
    })
  })

  # ---- Join observed + predicted ----
  df <- left_join(df_obs, df_pred, by = c("id", "fishery", "length")) %>%
    select(-year.y) %>%
    rename(year = year.x)

  # ---- Plot fishery 1 (Comm) ----
  yrs_plot_1 <- seq(from=11,to=81,by=10)
  p1 <- ggplot(df %>% filter(fishery == "1", year %in% yrs_plot_1), aes(x = length)) +
    geom_col(aes(y = obs), fill = "grey70", width = 2) +
    geom_line(data = df_sim_all %>% filter(fishery == "1", year %in% yrs_plot_1),
              aes(y = sim, group = sim_id), colour = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3, linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_line(aes(y = pred), colour = "red3", linewidth = 0.7) +
    facet_wrap(~ year, scales = "free_y", ncol = 5) +
    labs(x = "Length (cm)", y = "Proportion",
         title = "Length composition: Comm (Fishery 1)",
         subtitle = "Grey bars = observed, red = predicted, blue = simulated") +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 7),
          axis.text = element_text(size = 6))
  print(p1)
}

Model estimates

Visualise the selectivity curves by fleet (at length):

par_sel_est <- obj$env$parList()$par_sel

fleet_names <- c("Comm", "Non_comm", "ResFish")

sel_len_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(data$n_fishery), function(f) {
  par_f <- par_sel_est[f, ]
  sel_l <- if (data$sel_type_f[f] == 1L) {
    sel_logistic(data$len_mid, par_f)
  } else {
    sel_double_normal(data$len_mid, par_f)
  }
  data.frame(
    fishery    = f,
    fleet_name = fleet_names[f],
    length     = data$len_mid,
    selectivity = as.numeric(sel_l)
  )
}))

ggplot(sel_len_df, aes(x = length, y = selectivity)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~fleet_name, ncol = 3) +
  labs(x = "Length (cm)", y = "Selectivity") +
  ylim(0, 1)

Visualise the selectivity curves by fleet (at age):

rep <- obj$report()
sel_fya <- rep$sel_fya

sel_df <- expand.grid(fishery = 1:data$n_fishery, age = 1:data$n_age)
sel_df$selectivity <- sapply(1:nrow(sel_df), function(i) {
  sel_fya[sel_df$fishery[i], 1, sel_df$age[i]]
})
sel_df$real_age <- data$age_a[sel_df$age]
sel_df$fleet_name <- fleet_names[sel_df$fishery]

ggplot(sel_df, aes(x = real_age, y = selectivity)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~fleet_name, ncol = 3) +

Cross-platform comparison

Estimated spawning biomass

The figure below compares opal’s estimated spawning biomass trajectory (blue, with 95% confidence intervals) to three reference trajectories from SS3: the operating model truth (black), the SS3 estimation model with 3 growth platoons (red), and an SS3 estimation model without platoons (dark green). The SS3 EM without platoons provides the most direct comparison to opal, which uses a single growth track with continuous PLA integration rather than discrete platoons.

Opal’s estimated trajectory tracks the SS3 EM (no platoon) closely in shape, with a persistent negative bias in scale of approximately 10–20%. This bias is an estimation-level difference, not a structural dynamics error, as demonstrated by the dynamics diagnostic below.

spawning_biomass_est <- as.data.frame(summary(Report)[which(rownames(summary(Report)) == "spawning_biomass_y"), c("Estimate","Std. Error")])
colnames(spawning_biomass_est) <- c("estimate", "std_error")
spawning_biomass_est <- spawning_biomass_est[1:data$n_year,]
spawning_biomass_est$year <- calendar_years
spawning_biomass_est$lower <- spawning_biomass_est$estimate - 1.96 * spawning_biomass_est$std_error
spawning_biomass_est$upper <- spawning_biomass_est$estimate + 1.96 * spawning_biomass_est$std_error

# bring in true spawning biomass from the SS3 model (from the data object)
data(opaka_truth)

# prepare plotting limits
ybmax <- max(spawning_biomass_est$upper,
             obj$report()$spawning_biomass_y,
             opaka_truth$om$sprseries$SSB,
             opaka_truth$em$sprseries$SSB,
             na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot(spawning_biomass_est, aes(x = year)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = estimate), colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(data=subset(opaka_truth$om$sprseries, Yr %in% calendar_years), aes(x=Yr, y=SSB), colour = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(data=subset(opaka_truth$em$sprseries, Yr %in% calendar_years), aes(x=Yr, y=SSB), colour = "red", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Spawning biomass",
       title = "Estimated spawning biomass trajectory",
       subtitle = "Black = SS3 OM truth, Red = SS3 EM, Coloured = opal estimates") +
  # scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, ybmax * 1.2)) +
  theme_minimal()

Dynamics diagnostic

To understand where opal’s estimates differ from SS3, we build a sequence of four model variants that progressively relax constraints:

  1. obj (ASPM-R): The main opal assessment model structured as an age-structured production model (ASPM) and only fitting to the index. B0B_0, CPUE catchabilities, all 44 initial age-structure deviations (init_rdev_a), and 74 annual recruitment deviations (rdev_y) are freely estimated. Selectivity is computed through opal’s PLA mechanism using SS3-derived length selectivity parameters.

  2. obj_check_nosel (PLA selectivity; scale fixed): All parameters are fixed at SS3’s MLE values, with selectivity computed via opal’s probability-of-length-at-age (PLA) integration. If the trajectory matches SS3, any remaining gap in obj is an estimation-level difference.

  3. obj_check (SS3 selectivity; scale fixed): Same as above but with SS3’s exact age-selectivity matrix (from the AGE_SELEX report) injected directly, bypassing PLA. Comparing to obj_check_nosel reveals how much of any gap is attributable to the PLA approximation vs. other model structure.

  4. obj_est (PLA selectivity; scale estimated): Starting from SS3’s MLE values, B0B_0 and CPUE catchabilities are freely re-estimated while all other parameters (growth, selectivity, recruitment deviations) remain fixed at SS3 values. This isolates the effect of estimating scale from the SS3 MLE starting point.

# ---- Dynamics diagnostic: fix all parameters at SS3 MLE values ----
# This isolates opal's population dynamics from estimation differences.
# If the forward projection matches SS3, the dynamics are correct and any
# gap in the estimated model is due to parameter estimation (different
# likelihood surface, selectivity parameterization, etc.). If the projection
# doesn't match, a structural issue remains.

# SS3 MLE values from ss.par and derived quantities
# SS3's SSB_Virgin = 4785.86, ln(R0) = 5.67638520257, h = 0.76, sigma_r = 0.52

                     parameters = parameters_ss3,
                     map = map_est)

# Parameter bounds (relevant parameters only)
Lwr <- rep(-Inf, length(obj_est$par))
Upr <- rep(Inf, length(obj_est$par))
Lwr[grep("log_B0", names(obj_est$par))] <- log(1)
Upr[grep("log_B0", names(obj_est$par))] <- log(exp(22))
Lwr[grep("rdev_y", names(obj_est$par))] <- rep(-5, length(grep("rdev_y", names(obj_est$par))))
Upr[grep("rdev_y", names(obj_est$par))] <- rep(5, length(grep("rdev_y", names(obj_est$par))))
Lwr[grep("init_rdev_a", names(obj_est$par))] <- rep(-5, data$n_age)
Upr[grep("init_rdev_a", names(obj_est$par))] <- rep(5, data$n_age)
Lwr[grep("log_init_F_f", names(obj_est$par))] <- log(1e-12)
Upr[grep("log_init_F_f", names(obj_est$par))] <- log(3)

# Optimize (2-stage run for stability)
control <- list(eval.max = 10000, iter.max = 10000)
opt_est <- nlminb(start = obj_est$par, objective = obj_est$fn,
                  gradient = obj_est$gr, lower = Lwr, upper = Upr,
                  control = control)
opt_est <- nlminb(start = opt_est$par, objective = obj_est$fn,
                  gradient = obj_est$gr, lower = Lwr, upper = Upr,
                  control = control)

cat("estimation convergence:", opt_est$convergence, "\n")
cat("max gradient:", max(abs(obj_est$gr())), "\n")

Model with length compositions

The ASPM-R model (obj) estimated B0B_0, CPUE catchabilities, and initial age-structure deviations, but held selectivity fixed at SS3’s MLE values. Turning on the length composition likelihood allows the data to inform selectivity directly and relaxes that constraint.

The new model (obj_lf) extends obj with two additional changes:

  • lf_switch = 1L (multinomial): length composition observations from Comm (fleet 1, 1949–2023) and ResFish (fleet 3, 2017–2023) enter the likelihood.
  • Selectivity estimated for fleets 1 and 3: the two logistic parameters for Comm and all six double-normal parameters for ResFish are freed. Fleet 2 (Non_comm) retains its fixed SS3 selectivity as it has no LF data.

All other parameters match obj: σR\sigma_R, steepness, and growth remain fixed at SS3 values; B0B_0, catchabilities, rdev_y, and init_rdev_a are freely estimated.

Setup 

# data_no_sel has no sel_fa_external (set in dynamics-check); use it as base
data_lf <- data_no_sel
data_lf$lf_switch <- 1L

map_sel <- matrix(NA, nrow(parameters$par_sel), ncol(parameters$par_sel))
map_sel[1,1:2 ] <- c(1,2) # Comm fleet selectivity parameters
map_sel[3,c(1,4,6) ] <- c(3,4,5) # Comm fleet selectivity parameters
map_sel = as.vector(map_sel)

map_lf <- map
map_lf$par_sel <- factor(map_sel)

Build the AD object 

obj_lf <- MakeADFun(func = cmb(opal_model, data_lf),
                    parameters = parameters,
                    map = map_lf)
unique(names(obj_lf$par))
obj_lf$fn()   # should be finite

Parameter bounds 

Lwr_lf <- rep(-Inf, length(obj_lf$par))
Upr_lf <- rep( Inf, length(obj_lf$par))

Lwr_lf[grep("log_B0",      names(obj_lf$par))] <- log(1)
Upr_lf[grep("log_B0",      names(obj_lf$par))] <- log(exp(22))
Lwr_lf[grep("log_cpue_q",  names(obj_lf$par))] <- log(0.001)
Upr_lf[grep("log_cpue_q",  names(obj_lf$par))] <- log(10)
Lwr_lf[grep("rdev_y",      names(obj_lf$par))] <- -5
Upr_lf[grep("rdev_y",      names(obj_lf$par))] <-  5
Lwr_lf[grep("init_rdev_a", names(obj_lf$par))] <- -5
Upr_lf[grep("init_rdev_a", names(obj_lf$par))] <-  5
Lwr_lf[grep("par_sel",     names(obj_lf$par))] <- -7
Upr_lf[grep("par_sel",     names(obj_lf$par))] <-  7

Optimisation 

control <- list(eval.max = 10000, iter.max = 10000)
opt_lf <- nlminb(start = obj_lf$par, objective = obj_lf$fn,
                 gradient = obj_lf$gr, lower = Lwr_lf, upper = Upr_lf,
                 control = control)
opt_lf <- nlminb(start = opt_lf$par, objective = obj_lf$fn,
                 gradient = obj_lf$gr, lower = Lwr_lf, upper = Upr_lf,
                 control = control)
opt_lf <- nlminb(start = opt_lf$par, objective = obj_lf$fn,
                 gradient = obj_lf$gr, lower = Lwr_lf, upper = Upr_lf,
                 control = control)
cat("Convergence:", opt_lf$convergence, "\n")
cat("Max gradient:", max(abs(obj_lf$gr())), "\n")
obj_lf$report()$lp_prior
obj_lf$report()$lp_rec
sum(obj_lf$report()$lp_cpue)
sum(obj_lf$report()$lp_lf)
check_estimability(obj = obj_lf)

Parameter table

Selectivity comparison 

par_sel_lf  <- obj_lf$env$parList()$par_sel
par_sel_obj <- obj$env$parList()$par_sel

sel_comp_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(data_lf$n_fishery), function(f) {
  sel_lf_l <- if (data_lf$sel_type_f[f] == 1L) {
    sel_logistic(data_lf$len_mid, par_sel_lf[f, ])
  } else {
    sel_double_normal(data_lf$len_mid, par_sel_lf[f, ])
  }
  sel_obj_l <- if (data$sel_type_f[f] == 1L) {
    sel_logistic(data$len_mid, par_sel_obj[f, ])
  } else {
    sel_double_normal(data$len_mid, par_sel_obj[f, ])
  }
  rbind(
    data.frame(fleet = fleet_names[f], length = data_lf$len_mid,
               selectivity = as.numeric(sel_lf_l),  model = "opal (with LF)"),
    data.frame(fleet = fleet_names[f], length = data$len_mid,
               selectivity = as.numeric(sel_obj_l), model = "opal (ASPM-R)")
  )
}))

ggplot(sel_comp_df, aes(x = length, y = selectivity, colour = model)) +

       title = "Selectivity-at-length: ASPM-R vs model with LF",
       colour = NULL) +

  theme_minimal() +

Catch Curve

The catch-curve model uses the same parameter structure as the opal with LF model (selectivity estimated for Comm and ResFish, recruitment deviations freely estimated) but removes the CPUE index from the likelihood. Instead, information about population scale comes entirely from the length composition data and the catch history. Because catchability (qq) is not informed by any index, it is fixed at its SS3 MLE value to avoid an unidentified parameter.

Setup 

# Inherit lf_switch = 1L and prepared LF arrays from data_lf
data_cc <- data_lf
data_cc$cpue_switch <- 0L   # exclude CPUE from likelihood

# Fix log_cpue_q since it is unidentified without CPUE data
map_cc <- map_lf
map_cc$log_cpue_q <- factor(rep(NA, length(parameters$log_cpue_q)))

obj_cc <- MakeADFun(func = cmb(opal_model, data_cc),
                    parameters = parameters,
                    map = map_cc)
unique(names(obj_cc$par))
obj_cc$fn()   # should be finite

Parameter bounds 

Lwr_cc <- rep(-Inf, length(obj_cc$par))
Upr_cc <- rep( Inf, length(obj_cc$par))

Lwr_cc[grep("log_B0",      names(obj_cc$par))] <- log(1)
Upr_cc[grep("log_B0",      names(obj_cc$par))] <- log(exp(22))
Lwr_cc[grep("rdev_y",      names(obj_cc$par))] <- -5
Upr_cc[grep("rdev_y",      names(obj_cc$par))] <-  5
Lwr_cc[grep("init_rdev_a", names(obj_cc$par))] <- -5
Upr_cc[grep("init_rdev_a", names(obj_cc$par))] <-  5
Lwr_cc[grep("par_sel",     names(obj_cc$par))] <- -7
Upr_cc[grep("par_sel",     names(obj_cc$par))] <-  7

Optimisation 

control <- list(eval.max = 10000, iter.max = 10000)
opt_cc <- nlminb(start = obj_cc$par, objective = obj_cc$fn,
                 gradient = obj_cc$gr, lower = Lwr_cc, upper = Upr_cc,
                 control = control)
opt_cc <- nlminb(start = opt_cc$par, objective = obj_cc$fn,
                 gradient = obj_cc$gr, lower = Lwr_cc, upper = Upr_cc,
                 control = control)
opt_cc <- nlminb(start = opt_cc$par, objective = obj_cc$fn,
                 gradient = obj_cc$gr, lower = Lwr_cc, upper = Upr_cc,
                 control = control)
cat("Convergence:", opt_cc$convergence, "\n")
cat("Max gradient:", max(abs(obj_cc$gr())), "\n")
obj_cc$report()$lp_prior
obj_cc$report()$lp_rec
sum(obj_cc$report()$lp_lf)

Diagnostics 

get_par_table(obj_cc, parameters, map_cc,
              lower = Lwr_cc, upper = Upr_cc, grad_tol = 1e-2, digits = 2L,
              include = "all_est")
check_estimability(obj = obj_cc)

Final summary

This section collects the four summary plots across all primary model variants: ASPM (index only, no recruitment deviations), ASPM-R (index only, recruitment deviations estimated), catch curve (LF only, no CPUE), and opal with LF (index + LF, selectivity estimated). SS3 OM and SS3 EM trajectories are included in the biomass panel for reference.

A shared colour palette is used throughout:

summary_colours <- c(
  "ASPM"           = "#E69F00",  # amber
  "ASPM-R"         = "purple",
  "Catch curve"    = "darkorange",
  "opal (with LF)" = "cyan4",
  "SS3 OM"         = "black",
  "SS3 EM"         = "red"
)

CPUE fits

CPUE predicted trajectories for ASPM, ASPM-R, and opal with LF. The catch curve is excluded as it does not fit the CPUE index.

make_cpue_df <- function(obj, model_label, cpue_data) {
  cpue_data %>%
    mutate(pred  = obj$report()$cpue_pred,
           model = model_label)
}

cpue_summary <- bind_rows(
  make_cpue_df(obj_aspm, "ASPM",           data_aspm$cpue_data),
  make_cpue_df(obj,      "ASPM-R",          data$cpue_data),
  make_cpue_df(obj_lf,   "opal (with LF)", data_lf$cpue_data)
)

ggplot(cpue_summary, aes(x = ts)) +
  geom_point(data = cpue_summary %>% filter(model == "ASPM-R"),
             aes(y = value, fill = factor(index)),
             shape = 21, size = 2.5) +
  geom_line(aes(y = pred, colour = model, linetype = factor(index)),
            linewidth = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = summary_colours) +
  scale_fill_brewer(type = "qual", palette = "Dark2") +
  facet_wrap(~index, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y",
             labeller = labeller(index = c("1" = "Index 1 (Comm)", "2" = "Index 2 (Survey)"))) +
  labs(x = "Time step", y = "CPUE", colour = "Model", fill = "Index",
       linetype = "Index",
       title = "Summary: CPUE fits",
       subtitle = "Points = observed; lines = model predictions") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

Length composition fits

Observed length compositions (grey bars) with predicted proportions from opal with LF (cyan) and the catch curve (orange). Shown for Comm (decadal subset) and all ResFish years.

# Build long-format predicted LF for both models, labelled
build_lf_pred_df <- function(obj_x, data_x, model_label) {
  pred_list <- obj_x$report()$lf_pred
  names(pred_list) <- data_x$lf_fishery_f
  for (k in seq_along(pred_list)) colnames(pred_list[[k]]) <- data_x$len_mid
  yr_list <- split(data_x$lf_year, data_x$lf_fishery)
  map_dfr(seq_along(pred_list), function(i) {
    m   <- pred_list[[i]]
    yrs <- yr_list[[i]]
    as.data.frame.table(m, responseName = "pred", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
      rename(id = Var1, length = Var2) %>%
      mutate(fishery   = as.character(names(pred_list)[i]),
             id        = as.integer(factor(id, levels = unique(id))),
             year      = yrs[id],
             cal_year  = 1948L + year,
             length    = as.numeric(length),
             model     = model_label)
  })
}

df_pred_sum_lf <- build_lf_pred_df(obj_lf, data_lf, "opal (with LF)")
df_pred_sum_cc <- build_lf_pred_df(obj_cc, data_cc, "Catch curve")
df_pred_summary <- bind_rows(df_pred_sum_lf, df_pred_sum_cc)

# Observed (use data_lf; same obs for both models)

  group_by(fishery) %>% mutate(id = row_number()) %>% ungroup() %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(year, fishery, id), names_to = "length", values_to = "obs") %>%
  mutate(length = as.numeric(length), cal_year = 1948L + year)

# Comm: decadal years

Dynamic depletion

Dynamic depletion (Bt/B0,dynamicB_t / B_{0,\text{dynamic}}) for each opal model variant. The SS3 OM and SS3 EM are not shown as their depletion is defined relative to a different reference point and is not directly comparable to opal’s dynamic_depletion_y metric.

dep_summary <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(year = calendar_years,
             depletion = obj_aspm$report()$dynamic_depletion_y[1:data$n_year],
             model = "ASPM"),
  data.frame(year = calendar_years,
             depletion = obj$report()$dynamic_depletion_y[1:data$n_year],
             model = "ASPM-R"),
  data.frame(year = calendar_years,
             depletion = rep_cc$dynamic_depletion_y[1:data$n_year],
             model = "Catch curve"),
  data.frame(year = calendar_years,
             depletion = rep_lf$dynamic_depletion_y[1:data$n_year],
             model = "opal (with LF)")
)

ggplot(dep_summary, aes(x = year, y = depletion, colour = model)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.4, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = summary_colours) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = expression(B[t] / B[0*","*dynamic]),
       title = "Summary: dynamic depletion trajectories",
       subtitle = "Dashed line = 40% depletion reference",
       colour = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
